about: Millbrook Vineyards & Winery is the Hudson Valley estate John Dyson founded on a former dairy farm outside the village of Millbrook in Dutchess County. Dyson, a former New York Commissioner of Agriculture and Markets, bought the 130-acre farm in 1982 and, with encouragement from Finger Lakes pioneer Dr. Konstantin Frank, planted vinifera in 1983. Pinot Noir and Chardonnay were among those first plantings, and the vineyard has since grown to about 30 acres. The first vintage came in 1985.

Millbrook’s Pinot Noir comes from the estate vineyard and from Long Island growers, and is bottled under the New York State appellation. Winemaker Ian Beaurup now leads the cellar after the retirement of John Graziano, who made the wines for decades. He arrived from Balletto Vineyards in Sonoma County, with earlier stints in Oregon and New Zealand, so cool-climate Pinot Noir is home ground for him.

The winery describes deep aromas of dark berries, raspberry and black currant, with a note of soft rose petals, followed by cherry and plum on the palate, soft tannins and a smooth finish. As one Hudson Valley writer has noted, buying it at the winery is part of the fun, and the region’s cooler climate gives a more delicate, less fruit-heavy Pinot Noir than California’s, a style that suits the table.
